top5.title: ChatGPT Reaches 20% of Google’s Search Volume
top5.description: According to Adam Fry of OpenAI, ChatGPT now handles approximately one-fifth of the number of search-like queries handled by Google. ChatGPT would therefore be ahead of Bing, which holds about 5% of the search market.
top5.why: ChatGPT reaching roughly 20% of Google’s search volume signals a potentially major shift in how users discover information and where search advertising may flow.

top5.title: Meta Seeks to Raise Up to $25 Billion in Debt to Fund AI
top5.description: Meta is seeking to raise up to $25 billion in the debt markets as its artificial intelligence spending increases.
top5.why: Meta seeking up to $25 billion in debt underscores the extraordinary scale of AI infrastructure spending and the growing reliance on financial markets to fund it.

top5.title: U.S. Voters Reject Dozens of AI Data Centers
top5.description: During the midterm elections, U.S. voters approved 33 measures limiting AI data center projects, while six others were leading. The measures range from permanent bans to moratoriums and power limits.
top5.why: Voters approving dozens of measures restricting AI data centers shows that power, water and local opposition are becoming material constraints on the industry’s expansion.

top5.title: Apple Opens Siri’s AI to All Apps
top5.description: Apple now allows app developers to integrate their content and actions with Siri through a developer preview. Integrations could include checking a delivery, booking a service, or combining multiple actions.
top5.why: Opening Siri to app actions could turn Apple’s assistant into a broad agentic interface for transactions and services across the iPhone ecosystem.

top5.title: Google Threatens to Cut Off Search for Schools That Ban AI
top5.description: Google plans to remove Search access from student accounts managed by schools that reject its AI tools. Beginning in early 2027, institutions will also have to manually enable several AI features that are disabled by default.
top5.why: Google tying Search access to schools’ acceptance of its AI tools raises significant questions about corporate leverage over education, platform access and AI policy.
